questions.question: What is the highest common factor of 48, 120 and 240?
questions.solution:
Prime factors of 48 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 2 × 24

Prime factors of 120 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 = 5 × 24

Prime factors of 240 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 = 10 × 24

⇒ highest common factor of 48, 120 and 240 is 24

questions.question: While working 5 hours a day, X alone can cut 15 trees in 9 days. In how many days X can cut 40 trees working 8 hours a day?
questions.solution:
X’s 9 - day work, working 5 hours a day = 15

X’s one day work working 5 hours a day = 15/9

X’s 1 hour work = 15/(9 × 5) = 1/3

X’s 3 hour work = 1/3 × 3 = 1

It take 3 hours by X to cut one tree.

It will take (3 × 40 = 120) hours to cut 40 trees.

Working 8 hours a day,

X will take 120/8 days

∴ X will take 15 days to cut 40 trees working 8 hours a day.

**Shortcut method:**

MADAHAEA/WA = MBDBHBEB/WB(1)

Where, M = no of men

D = no of days

H = hours per day

W = amount of work

E = Efficiency

Here MA = MB = 1

WA = 15

WB = 40

HA = 5

HB = 8

DA = 9

DB = ?

EA = E**B**

Using equation (1)

(1 × 9 × 5)/15 = (1 × DB × 8)/40

⇒ 3 = DB/5

⇒ DB = 15

X can cut 40 trees working 8 hours a day in 15 days.

questions.question: Marked price of an article is Rs 7500. It is purchased at a discount of 12%. If Rs. 250 are spent on its repairs, then to gain 20% profit what should be the selling price (in Rs)?
questions.solution:
Marked price = M.P = Rs. 7500

After discount of 12%

Purchased price = (1 - 0.12) × 7500 = Rs. 6600

After spending Rs. 250 on repair

Cost price = C.P = Rs. (6600 + 250) = Rs. 6850

To gain a profit of 20%

Selling price = (1 + 0.20) × C.P = 1.2 × 6850 = Rs. 8220

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling price = (1 + profit percent/100) × {(1 - discount percent/100) × marked price + repair cost}

Selling price = 1.2 × {(1 - 0.12) × 7500 + 250} = Rs. 8220

questions.question: After giving a discount of 33.33%, there is a loss of 11.111%. If only 10% discount is given, then what will be the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
Let the marked price (M.P) = x

After a discount of 33.33%

Selling price = S.P = (1 - 0.3333) × x = 0.6667x

Loss percentage = (loss/C.P) × 100 = {(C.P - S.P)/C.P} × 100

Loss% = 11.111%

⇒ (C.P - 0.6667x)/C.P} × 100 = 11.111

⇒ 1 - 0.6667x/C.P = 0.11111

⇒ 0.6667x/C.P = 0.88889

⇒ C.P = 0.6667x/0.88889 = 0.75x

When only 10% discount was given

S.P = (1 - 0.1) × x = 0.9x

Profit = S.P - C.P = 0.9x - 0.75x = 0.15x

Profit% = (profit/C.P) × 100

⇒ profit % = (0.15x/0.75x) × 100 = 20%

**Alternate Solution:**

33.33% = 1/3

Ratio of MP to SP = 3: (3 - 1) = (3: 2) × 4 = 12: 8 ---(A)

11.11% = 1/9

Ratio of CP to SP = 9: (9 - 1) = (9: 8) × 1 = 9: 8 --- (B)

If discount is 10% then Ratio of MP to SP = 10: 9 ---- (C)

Make MP same in A and C, new ratio of A and C = 60 : 40 and 60: 54 Now making SP of B equal to new ratio of A, = 45: 40

So CP = 45 unit and SP = 54 unit

Profit = (9/45) × 100 = 20%

questions.question: In what ratio two types of liquid costing Rs. 52/litre and Rs. 65/litre should be mixed to obtain a mixture of Rs. 60/litre?
questions.solution:
Let x litre of liquid costing Rs. 52/litre be mixed with (1 - x) litre of liquid costing Rs. 65/litre making it a mixture of 1 litre

Cost of new liquid = (x) × 52 + (1 - x) × 65 = 65 - 13x

Cost of mixture = 60/litre

⇒ 65 - 13x = 60

⇒ 13x = 5

⇒ x = 5/13

⇒ (1 - x) = 1 - 5/13 = 8/13

The ratio in which liquids must be mixed = x/(1 - x) = (5/13)/(8/13) = 5/8 = 5∶ 8

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**

Quantity of cheaper/quantity of dearer = (price of dearer - mean price) / (mean price - price of cheaper)

Price of cheaper = Rs. 52/litres

Price of dearer = Rs. 65/litre

Mean price = Rs. 60/litre

Required ratio = Quantity of cheaper/quantity of dearer

Required ratio = (65 - 60)/(60 - 52) = 5/8 = 5 ∶ 8

questions.question: If the selling price of 10 articles is equal to the cost price of 15 articles, then what is the profit percent?
questions.solution:
Selling price = S.P

Cost price = C.P

Selling price of 10 articles = cost price of 15 articles

⇒ 10 S.P = 15 C.P

⇒ S.P = 1.5 C.P

Profit percentage = (profit/C.P) × 100 = {(S.P - C.P)/C.P} × 100 = {(1.5C.P - C.P)/C.P} × 100 = 0.5 × 100 = 50%

questions.question: A shopkeeper buys a fan for Rs 14500. For how much should he sell (in Rs) it to gain a profit of 10%?
questions.solution:
Cost price = C.P = Rs. 14500

profit % = (profit/C.P) × 100

⇒ 10 = (profit/14500) × 100

Profit = (10 × 14500)/100 = 1450

Profit = S.P - C.P

S.P = sell price

⇒ S.P = profit + C.P = 1450 + 14500 = Rs. 15950

**Shortcut method:**

Profit = 10%

Selling price = (1 + profit percent/100) × cost price

Selling price = (1 + 10/100) × 14500 = 1.1 × 14500 = Rs.15950

questions.question: The difference between 81% and 49% of a number is 768. What is the 48% of the number?
questions.solution:
Let the number be x

81% of x = 0.81x

49% of x = 0.49x

Difference between 81% of x and 49% of x = 768

⇒ 0.81x - 0.49x = 768

⇒ 0.32x = 768

⇒ x = 2400

48% of x = 0.48x = 0.48 × 2400 = 1152

questions.question: If the side of a cube increases by 15%, then what will be the percentage increase in the volume of the cube?
questions.solution:
Let the sides of the cube be a m

Volume of cube = a³m³

When side is increased by 15%

New side = 1.15a

New volume = (1.15a)³ = 1.5208 a³

Increase in volume = new volume - volume = 1.5208 a³ - a³ = 0.5208 a³

Percentage increase in volume = (change in volume/volume) × 100 = (0.5208a³/a³) × 100 = 52.08 %

questions.question: A train crosses a platform in 30 seconds travelling with a speed of 72 km/hr. If the length of the train be 120 metres, then what will be the length (in metres) of the platform?
questions.solution:
Speed = distance/time

Distance = speed × time

Speed = 72 km/hr

Time = 30 sec = 30/(60 × 60) = 1/120 hr

Distance travelled by train in 30 sec = 72 × (1/120) = 0.6 km = 600m

Distance travelled by train = length of platform + length of train

⇒ length of platform = 600 - 120 = 480 m

**Shortcut method:**

Length of platform = (speed × time) - length of train

⇒ length of platform = {72 × (30/3600)} - 120/1000 = 0.48 km = 480 m

questions.question: The speed of a boat is 3 km/hr in still water and the speed of the stream is 1 km/hr. If the boat takes 9 hours to go to a place and come back, then what is the distance (in km) of the place?
questions.solution:
Speed of boat in still water = B = 3 km/hr

Speed of stream = S = 1 km/hr

Speed of boat going downstream = B + S = 3 + 1 = 4 km/hr

Speed of boat going upstream = B - S = 3 - 1 = 2 km/hr

Let the distance of the place be d.

Time taken to go to that place = Distance/Speed of boat downstream = d/4 hr

Time taken to come back from that place = Distance/Speed of boat upstream = d/2 hr

Total time taken to go and come back to that place = 9 hr

⇒ d/4 + d/2 = 9

⇒ 3d/4 = 9

⇒ d = 12 km

⇒ (P × 12 × 3)/100 = 720

⇒ P × 0.36 = 720

questions.question: The marks obtained by P in test 3 is how much percent more than the marks obtained by P in test 2?
questions.solution:
Maximum marks = 200

Marks obtained by P in test 2 = 120

Marks obtained by P in test 3 = 140

Difference in marks obtained = 140 - 120 = 20

∴ Percentage difference of marks obtained in test 3 with respect to test 2 = (difference in marks/marks in test 2) × 100 = (20/120) × 100 = 16.66%

questions.question: What is the average marks obtained by Q in the given 5 tests?
questions.solution:
Average marks of Q = (total marks in all subject)/(total number of subject)

Average marks of Q = (115 + 170 + 110 + 175 + 95)/5 = 665/5 = 133

questions.question: The total marks obtained by P are how much less than the total marks obtained by Q in the five tests?
questions.solution:
Total marks obtained by P in all subjects = 145 + 120 + 140 + 150 + 105 = 660

Total marks obtained by Q in all subjects = 115 + 170 + 110 + 175 + 95 = 665

Difference in marks = 665 - 660 = 5

The total marks obtained by P is 5 less than total marks obtained by Q.
